 Caleb Wilson 
 CHI 
 Forward

 Player Stats

 Caleb Wilson had 21 points (7-of-14 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, one assist, one steal, two blocks and two three-pointers against the Bucks on Friday. 
 After Wilson’s inauspicious debut Wednesday that included 33.3 percent shooting from the field and nine turnovers, the 20-year-old forward bounced back nicely in the second game of his NBA career. He was 7-of-14 from the field (50 percent), scored 21 points and had just three turnovers. Wilson will have ups and downs in his career and there will certainly be more bumps in the road during his rookie season, but this was undoubtedly a promising performance. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Caleb Wilson notched 16 points (7-of-21 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, three steals, one block and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Raptors. 
 Regardless of position, efficiency can be an issue for rookies, and that was certainly the case for Wilson in his official NBA debut. In addition to shooting 33.3 percent from the field, the lottery pick out of North Carolina racked up nine turnovers. Wilson will be a high-usage player this season, but that may hurt his fantasy value, especially for those who can’t afford a major drop in field-goal percentage or an increase in turnovers. The good news is that the rookie has better nights ahead, because Scottie Barnes and Kawhi Leonard are challenging matchups for any wing. 
 Caleb Wilson 
 CHI 
 Forward 
 Caleb Wilson puts up 16 points (7-of-15 FGs), 7 rebounds, 4 assists, 2 blocks and two 3-pointers against the Timberwolves 
 Caleb Wilson has been as advertised in the pre-season. It will not take long for him to be the best player on the Bulls. The highlight reel bias with Wilson will be very strong this year, so he will be a candidate to sell high in certain situations because of the high scoring and flashy dunks. 
 Caleb Wilson 
 CHI 
 Forward 
 Caleb Wilson finished Sunday’s exhibition against the Nuggets with 17 points (6-of-10 FGs, 4-of-7 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, one block and one three-pointer. 
 After logging 32 minutes in Friday’s exhibition against the Grizzlies, Wilson played 17 on Sunday. The rookie forward committed five turnovers, but his shooting improved when compared to his 7-of-17 night against Memphis. With the Bulls rebuilding, Wilson will have a lot of leeway on offense, and he should be one of the NBA’s top rookies. Fantasy managers will simply hope that efficiency won’t be too much of an issue. 
 Caleb Wilson 
 CHI 
 Forward 
 Caleb Wilson had 21 points (7-of-17 FGs, 2-of-6 FTs), four rebounds, one steal and five three-pointers against the Grizzlies on Friday. 
 Wilson started and played 32 minutes, which was the most of anyone on either team. The 20-year-old forward who was the fourth overall pick in the draft had 21 points on 17 attempts. He bounced back after missing all four of his three-point attempts in his last preseason game to make 5-of-11 threes against the Grizzlies. Wilson is an intriguing pick with upside in the top-75 of fantasy drafts this year. 
 Caleb Wilson 
 CHI 
 Forward 
 Caleb Wilson finished Wednesday’s exhibition against the Suns with 15 points (6-of-15 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, two assists and one steal. 
 Wilson made his unofficial Bulls debut as a starter, and he should keep that role once the regular season begins. The rookie didn’t have a good night from deep, missing all four of his three-point attempts, but that’s an area where he performed better than expected during Summer League. Playing off a point guard like Josh Giddey should give Wilson ample transition opportunities, potentially offsetting any perimeter shooting concerns. 
 Caleb Wilson 
 CHI 
 Forward 
 Caleb Wilson notched 21 points (7-of-15 FGs, 3-of-5 FTs), eight rebounds, two assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Thursday’s loss to the Lakers. 
 Wilson may have shot the ball reasonably well on Thursday, but this was his worst showing in Las Vegas by some distance. More damaging than the 1-of-6 day from beyond the arc was the turnover count, as the lottery pick was responsible for eight. Wilson has said he does not plan to sit at all, but the Bulls will have nothing to play for in their fifth and final game. And his absence could create opportunities for fellow first-round pick Dailyn Swain (four points, two rebounds, one assist, and one steal), who has struggled throughout Chicago’s time in Las Vegas. 
 Caleb Wilson 
 CHI 
 Forward 
 Caleb Wilson finished Tuesday’s win over the Wizards with 19 points (7-of-15 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), eight rebounds, two assists, one block and two three-pointers. 
 After losses in his first two summer league games, Wilson got his first victory on Tuesday. The showdown between him and AJ Dybantsa never materialized, as the Wizards shut down the first overall pick, as well as Tre Johnson and Will Riley. Wilson knocked down two more three-pointers, and the perimeter shot that was his big weakness going into the draft has been an asset in Las Vegas. With the Bulls rebuilding and clearly viewing him as a key building block, one can make a case for Wilson being the first rookie off the board in drafts this fall. 
 Caleb Wilson 
 CHI 
 Forward 
 Caleb Wilson finished Monday’s loss to the Jazz with 19 points (8-of-17 FGs, 0-of-6 FTs), eight rebounds, two assists, two steals, five blocks and three three-pointers. 
 After going off for 35 points in his summer league debut, Wilson was bound to slow down some. That’s precisely what happened, as the Bulls forward started slowly. However, he would do more than score against the Jazz, with the final stat line including two steals and five blocked shots. In fantasy basketball, defensive production can compensate for offensive struggles, so that was good to see from Wilson. The negative from his performance on Monday was the 0-of-6 night at the foul line. Wilson is now 2-of-12 from the charity stripe in Las Vegas, but this should not be a long-term concern for fantasy managers. 
 Caleb Wilson 
 CHI 
 Forward 
 Caleb Wilson tallied 35 points (12-of-21 FGs, 2-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, two steals, three blocks and seven three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Grizzlies. 
 What a night for Wilson, who set the franchise record for most points in a summer league debut. While there were some negatives, most notably the six turnovers, Wilson’s shot-making ability was highly impressive. He shot 7-of-11 from beyond the arc, including one as time expired. Given his perimeter shooting struggles during his lone season at North Carolina, it would be a game-changer for Wilson and the Bulls if he can consistently hit those shots once the games count. 
 Leonard Miller 
 CHI 
 Forward 
 #11 
 According to Hoops Hype’s Michael Scotto, the Bulls have guaranteed Leonard Miller’s contract for the 2026-27 season. 
 Three days after it was reported that the Bulls picked up Miller’s contract option for next season, they have now fully guaranteed it. A double-digit scorer in 17 of his final 18 games, the 2023 second-round pick averaged 11.7 points, 5.8 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.1 three-pointers per game after joining the Bulls as part of the trade that sent Ayo Dosunmu to Minnesota. While the contract does give Miller some security, his chances of affecting fantasy basketball aren’t great after the Bulls used one of their two first-round picks on Caleb Wilson in the draft.

 Leonard Miller had 19 points (7-of-11 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, two assists, one block and two three-pointers against the Bucks on Friday. 
 Miller only played 23 minutes off the bench in this one as Caleb Wilson and Norman Powell were the only Bulls to play at least 30 minutes. Still, it’s impossible to ignore Miller’s production after an impressive preseason and the first two games of the regular season. He’s scored in double figures in both games despite minutes totals in the low-20s. Miller probably needs more minutes to be fantasy-relevant, but at some point he could force his way into a more prominent role in the rotation.

 The Charlotte Hornets will start Dennis Schroeder, Sion James, Brandon Miller, Naz Reid, and Moussa Diabate against the the Hawks on Friday. 
 Despite Grayson Allen having a real good game on Wednesday, Sion James is still the starter for this game. Given that Sion did start 19 games last year, it seems like he will stay in the starting lineup until players return to help balance out the starters.  Norman Powell had 25 points (7-of-20 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), four rebounds, one assist and two three-pointers in the Bulls’ 132-125 victory over the Hawks on Friday. 
 Powell was the Bulls’ leading scorer in the victory over the Bucks on Wednesday. While he had 25 points, Powell’s typically excellent shooting from behind the three-point line was noticeably absent. The 33-year-old shooting guard went 2-of-12 from behind the arc and is now 4-of-18 (22.2 percent) from long distance this season. Powell is a career 39.6 percent three-point shooter and should have better shooting games in his future as he’s due for positive regression.
